title: Trace-driven certification on complete public revision histories
status: Frozen before any revision metadata for this study was requested. Later changes require a new protocol version; the analysis must follow this file.
question: How often does equality of a content hash hide an intervening change, and what do certification rules that rely on content hashes, on revision identifiers, or on the exact pairwise rule certify on real histories?

source.client: Serial requests, at least 2 s apart, maxlag=5, descriptive User-Agent without personal contact data, raw responses frozen with SHA-256.

vital.frame: Namespace-0 links on the page 'Wikipedia:Vital articles/Level 3', taken from the link table at collection time; the page revision ID reported with the links is recorded.
vital.selection: Sort the distinct linked titles; draw 150 with random.Random(20261105).sample. Titles are resolved through redirects when histories are requested.

random.selection: The first 150 distinct page IDs returned by successive list=random requests (rnlimit=50). MediaWiki's page_random ordering supplies the randomness; the returned list is frozen.

history_model.state: The current revision of a page at second t is the latest revision whose timestamp is at most t; ties within one second are ordered by revid and a revision superseded within the same second has no positive duration.
history_model.window_start: The parent of the first in-window revision, fetched by revision ID, is current from window start until the first in-window revision. A page without such a parent is absent until its first revision.
history_model.body_identity: sha1 as reported by the API. A page with any hidden or missing sha1 in the window is excluded from all measurements and listed.
history_model.sound_identity: revid of the current revision. Revisions are only appended in the frozen list, so a displaced revid never becomes current again within the reconstructed history; this is a property of the frozen log, not a claim about every administrative operation.

measurements.M0_descriptive: Pages, revisions in window, pages with at least one content-hash return, number of return events (consecutive appearances of one sha1 separated by at least one different current state), and the duration of each departure (first different state to return).

M1_hidden_change.capture_times: t_k = window_start + 3600k seconds, k = 0, 1, ..., for every k with t_k + gap < window_end.
M1_hidden_change.pairs: Only pairs where the page exists at both instants.
M1_hidden_change.events: E_hash: equal sha1 at t_k and t_k+gap. H: some state current for positive duration in (t_k, t_k+gap] has a different sha1 or is absent. E_id: equal revid.
M1_hidden_change.report: Per stratum and gap: counts of pairs, E_hash, E_hash and H, E_id and H; the ratio P(H | E_hash) with a page-clustered percentile bootstrap 95% interval (2000 resamples of pages, random.Random(7)).

M2_bundles.pages_eligible: Pages that exist throughout the window.
M2_bundles.randomness: random.Random(seed) with seed = 1000*n + stratum_index, stratum_index vital=1, random=2; bundle membership, read order, start times and read instants are drawn from this generator in that order.
M2_bundles.schedule: Request j starts at t0 + j*gap and its read window is [t0 + j*gap, t0 + j*gap + 1]; the true read instant is uniform in the window. Double-collect methods read the permuted bundle 1..n then n..1 (2n requests); the exact rule reads 1..n-1, n, n-1..1 (2n-1 requests).

methods.hash_bridge: Certify if each page's two reads return equal sha1 and max first-read window end < min last-read window start.
methods.id_exact: Certify if each page read twice returns equal revid and first-window end <= last-window start holds for every ordered pair of distinct pages (the singly read page uses its one window for both).

ground_truth.claimed_interval: Bridge methods: [max first-window end, min last-window start). Exact rule: [max over twice-read pages of first-window end, min over twice-read pages of last-window start], which contains the single read's window.
ground_truth.G1_existential: Some instant in the claimed interval (or, for the exact rule, the true instant of the single read) at which every page has its observed sha1.
ground_truth.G2_continuity: Every twice-read page has its observed sha1 throughout [first true read instant, last true read instant].
ground_truth.report: Per stratum, n, gap and method: runs, certified runs, certified runs violating G1, certified runs violating G2.

interpretation_limits: Revision metadata describe source text at the raw-source resource, not rendered HTML, templates, caches or deployment.
The vital stratum is a curated frame and the random stratum follows MediaWiki's random ordering; neither is a sample of the Web.
Simulated captures use the frozen histories as ground truth; no request is sent to Wikipedia at the simulated times.
